note: The atlas's own Turkish translation of the Theogony, made from Evelyn-White's Greek (Loeb, 1914) line for line: each line renders the Greek line it is keyed by, though within a sentence a word may move to a neighbouring line, as Turkish word order asks. Drafted with Claude (Anthropic) on 2026-11-14 and awaiting the editor's review. Names keep the Greek forms (Kronos, Uranos, Nyks), with the Turkish ones a reader knows (Afrodit, Girit, Kıbrıs); Hesiod's abstract personifications born of Eris are given in Turkish words (Zahmet, Unutuş, Açlık).
